title: Transform focus management system into productivity timer with manual distraction logging

requirements.text: Remove automatic focus session start on app launch - users must manually initiate sessions from the dashboard

quotes: remove the Focus Session Required from the starting of app and it should not open automaticaly
Remove auto-start: the app won't automatically begin a focus session on launch

acceptanceCriteria: App loads directly to dashboard without triggering a focus session
No automatic redirects to focus session page on launch
Users can navigate freely without being forced into a session

requirements.text: Implement customizable productivity timer with preset and custom work/break intervals (Pomodoro-style)

quotes: a browser-based productivity timer with distraction logging features
Productivity timer with customizable work/break intervals

acceptanceCriteria: Users can select preset durations (15, 25, 45 minutes) or enter custom times
Timer displays countdown with start, pause, and reset controls
Clear visual indication of work session vs break time
Option to configure break length after work sessions

requirements.text: Create manual distraction logging interface where users can record interruptions during focus sessions and categorize them by source (YouTube, Instagram, work apps, etc.)

quotes: Manual distraction logging - users can record when they get distracted and categorize the source
Manual distraction logging with category selection (YouTube, Instagram, productive apps, etc.)

acceptanceCriteria: Quick-access button during active focus session to log a distraction
Category picker with common distraction sources (social media, messaging, entertainment, work interruptions)
Optional notes field for additional context
Distraction entries timestamped and associated with current session
Backend stores distraction logs with category, timestamp, and session reference

requirements.text: Build activity classification system in backend that categorizes apps/websites as productive or distracting based on user-defined rules

quotes: Classification system: productive vs distracting activities

acceptanceCriteria: Backend stores classification rules mapping apps/sites to productive or distracting categories
Users can customize classifications through settings interface
Default classifications provided for common apps (VS Code=productive, YouTube=distracting)
Classification data persists across sessions

requirements.text: Implement transition tracking to record sequences of activity switches (e.g., VS Code → YouTube) and identify interruption patterns

quotes: You see what happened before YouTube
Transition tracking: records what interrupted focused work

acceptanceCriteria: Backend records transitions as pairs: (source_activity, destination_activity, timestamp)
System identifies repeated patterns (same transition occurring 3+ times)
Dashboard displays most common interruption sources
Transition data used to calculate distraction frequency metrics

requirements.text: Create session history and analytics dashboard showing past focus sessions, distraction patterns, and most frequent interruption sources over time

quotes: Session history and analytics to identify distraction patterns over time
Pattern detection to identify your most common distractions

acceptanceCriteria: History view lists all completed focus sessions with duration, distraction count, and score
Analytics section shows top distraction sources ranked by frequency
Visual charts displaying distraction trends over days/weeks
Transition matrix showing most common interruption pathways
Filterable date ranges for historical analysis

requirements.text: Implement burnout/fatigue scoring algorithm based on switching frequency between productive and distracting activities with weighted penalties for context switches

quotes: Burnout/fatigue scoring based on your switching behavior

acceptanceCriteria: Backend calculates fatigue score using formula: small penalty for productive↔productive switches, large penalty for productive→distracting switches, fragmentation penalty for distracting→distracting chains
Score updates in real-time as user logs distractions
Dashboard displays current fatigue level with visual indicator (low/medium/high)
Historical burnout trends shown in chart format

requirements.text: Measure and display session duration metrics to distinguish between real work (25+ min), browsing (5-10 min), and checking habits (10-40 sec repeated visits)

quotes: Measure how long they stay in that app

acceptanceCriteria: Track duration for each logged activity/distraction
Classify activities by duration pattern: sustained focus (25+ min), brief browsing (5-10 min), habit checking (<1 min repeated)
Analytics show distribution of time across duration categories
Identify habitual distractions based on repeated short-duration visits

constraints: All tracking must be self-reported by the user - no automatic browser tab monitoring or screen capture
Do not read message content, capture keystrokes, or inspect page content
Only collect: app name, domain name, time duration, and user-reported switching frequency
Preserve existing backend data structures for focus sessions and destructive visits
Do not modify immutable frontend paths: useInternetIdentity.ts, useInternetIdentity.tsx, useActor.ts, main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui
nonGoals: Automatic desktop app monitoring or system-level tracking
Browser extension that monitors active tabs without user interaction
Python desktop tracker or native OS integration
Real-time screen recording or content inspection
Reading personal data from messages, chats, or documents
